column3: Batch S-clean — **15 members** on `693638fc`, after a bisect split the red batch. `batch-s` (`#1160`) is superseded.  ## What the bisect found, cause → member  **`speed` — no member.** The CI row (`features-b` cold 216s → 458s, +112%) **does not reproduce on a quiet Sprite**: `cpu-avrac-let-stmt` 322s → 328s (**+1.9%**), a five-directory features-b subset 156s → 157s, and this batch 326/155. The CI row's neighbours in the same shard (`features-a`, `features-c`) were inside 20%, so it was **the cold item's contention in that run**, not a regression. The one real, reproducible cost is the **`sublang` phase, 8.0s → 12.6s cold**, owned by `#1116`+`#1129` — which are held.  **`census` — two groups, additive.** `#1116`+`#1129`: retains +1.0%, releases +1.65%, reclaims +3.7%, list_writes +3.9% (fails three counters alone). `#1118`: +1.4% retains, +2.4% list_writes. Sum reproduces the batch's totals. `#1157`+`#1062` are **neutral**.  **`keepers-b` (`voices`, `dogfooding-rules`) — `#1118`.** Its three rules landed with a hand-merged `DOGFOODING.md` bullet and a **stale `docs/VOICES.md`** (83 rules vs 80).  **`features-c` test — `#1062` alone**, red on its own commit: the case never declares `icon_dirs`, so `resolve.unresolved` was the only voice. Fixed here with a one-line change to its case.  ## Members `#1157` `#1135` `#1154` `#1038` `#1049` `#1060` `#1122` `#1124` `#1125` `#1126` `#1130` `#1136` `#970` `#989` `#1062` (+ the `#1062` case fix)  ## Held, with the exact reason - **`#1118`** — census (retains +1.4%, list_writes +2.4%) **and** both keeper refusals: regenerate `DOGFOODING.md`'s block and `docs/VOICES.md` to 83 rules, then pay `list_writes` or raise the budget deliberately. - **`#1116` + `#1129`** with their `beside` follow-up — census ×3 and the `sublang` cost; **a chain** (`dc64c7ca` alone does not compile).  ## Verified on a Sprite `fmt --check` 11/11 · annotations **179/179** · `keepers-b` green (only `ci-invariants`, which fails because a synced Sprite tree has no `.git` — the keeper needs git, the Sprite has none) · **census all five counters BELOW main** · speed 326/155.  ## The ceiling this measurement sets **Six members, at most one touching the compiler's own source.** Census slack is 1.5% per counter and one such member spends 2–4%; each census run is ~5 minutes and this split cost **12 runs**. One batch = one CI cycle only pays while the batch is green — a red batch of 18 costs a full cycle *per attempt* to find the culprit.    SPEED_ACCEPT: `speed.cpu-std-avrac-features-b-cold` reading 216s -> 466s here (and 216s -> 435s on #1169) is **runner inflation, not this branch**. Three independent measurements:  1. A lane bisected this batch in **12 runs on a quiet Sprite** and could not attribute the row to **any** member: `cpu-avrac-let-stmt` 322s -> 328s (**+1.9%**), a five-directory features-b subset 156s -> 157s. 2. In the same CI run **every** other cold row was inflated too: `std-core-warm` +67%, `std-diagnostics-cold` +36%, `std-ui-http-cold` +31%, `std-io-cold` +30%, `std-assets-cold` +38%. 3. `tools/speed_note.sh` already documents this behaviour in its own comment — *"nearly every cold step ran 30-130% over its baseline"* — and its guard is `grew >= 30s`, an **absolute** floor tuned for the 6s and 10s rows. A 216s baseline clears 30s of noise alone, so the guard cannot fire where it is most needed.  A real regression in one member moves **one or two** rows. Every cold row moving together by 30-130% is a degraded runner. The counters — the actual ratchet — are green: `census` retains/releases/reclaims/list_reads/list_writes all **below** main.  **Follow-up owed:** make the backstop judge a row against the run's **own median inflation** (relative), not the absolute 30s floor, so a uniformly slow runner stops failing one row by name.

(#1012's own base was #916; here it rides on top of all three.)  ## Receipts  - `ui-tty-r` (the 30 tty commits on main 3e84ff94, before this train): std-ui 819/819 tests, 46 programs proved, eval == native == expected, on a Sprite with a compiler built from that tree. - This train: std-ui reached the program tests; `loop_frames` (a tty program test) failed after the merge (3 walks for three timers due together, 0 frames for one turn). Fixed in the last two commits (below). The rerun of std-ui on this head was still running when the PR opened. ui-board and ui-browser have not been run on the train. - CI is the gate for the rest.  ## Conflict resolutions (what was decided, and why)  - **Makefile `.PHONY`** (#976 vs #916): the union of the two lists (`wasm-tasks-mutations`, `wasm-host-check` added to #916's). - **`tui/layout.av`** (#976 vs #916): #916's solver arms; `.Key -> []` kept, since the key primitive draws nothing. - **`runtime_reach_test.av`** (#961 vs main): #961's world-row doc and name list; the count is **83** = main's 79 + #961's 4 world rows. This is an inference and has not been run yet; if CI disagrees, the number is the thing to look at. - **`app/app.av`** (tty paint scheduling vs #976 owner tracking): fields are the union; `standing` stays #976's owner list, with `refused`, plus the tty's `dirty`, `holding`, `asked`, `framer`, `walks`, `frames`. `turn_of` flushes the screen the user saw (tty), then runs the owned turn (#976). - **`native/sources.av`:** the served loop turns by owner (#976) and the frame flush is the tty's (`on.flush()`). - **`headless/headless.av`** (#976's virtual-clock driver vs the tty's frame flush):   - `advance` keeps #976's driver and holds frames over a batch, showing one frame per instant (so timers due together are one paint, as the tty's loop did).   - `ran` answers `Msg.Frame` (a counted flush). Both are new code, written for this merge. - **`realize/html/element.av`:** #976's `lower_each` (crowding by order) over the tty's older signature.  ## Cut / not done  - The events series (`@host` seats, wire 12) is not in this train; it is the next one after #983. - ui-board and ui-browser not run here.

column3: Draft, DO NOT MERGE. Lead releases it.  ## What changed - `checks.yml`: `prepare` emits `full` (0 for a draft without the `full-ci` label). Heavy legs (`keepers-a`, `keepers-b`, `runtime-keep`, `seed-check`, `flow-gate`, `cache-attacks`, `suites`) and the objects/libs build are gated on it. `keepers-static`, `gate` and `codecs` run on drafts. - `test` refuses a light run by name (`NOT A VERDICT`, exit 1), the same way the `only` run does. The wall budget is skipped on a light run. - Triggers add `ready_for_review` and `labeled`. - `tools/ci_invariants.py`: new `light-draft` invariant, with fixtures (real workflow passes; an ungated heavy leg and a silent light refusal are refused). - `docs/2026_10_11_THE_PIPELINE.md`: a paragraph on the light draft.  ## Watcher and batcher No code change needed. The watcher never arms a draft; a readied PR's `test` is the latest run's. If the full run never starts, `test` is FAILURE and the watcher refuses by name. The batcher requires `test` SUCCESS, so it refuses a light run.  ## Not done Part 3 (sharding the ~9 min jobs) is not in this PR. Blockers: `suites (std-avrac)` has no file-half split; `keepers-a` has no target split; `cache-attacks` has `CACHE_ATTACKS` sections, but sharding changes job names and the wall ratchet reads rows by name.  ## Expected wall Ready run: unchanged, `prepare` ~7.5 min + the longest job (~9.3 min). Light draft: `prepare` + `gate`/`keepers-static`, no heavy queue.  ## Verification `make ci-invariants` clean (5 invariants), `make ci-verdict` clean, `make pr-watcher` self-test holds, `make keepers-static` exit 0, `make pipeline-doc` resolves.  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

column3: Two approved slices of docs/2026_10_16_FOLD_AND_MEANS.md, batched.  **1. The `@fold` engine** (lane `nodes-fold-design`, landing A). std-grammar gains `Seq.fold`/`seed`, `match_fold`, an `origin` param for exact spans, and per-turn label/list/validator scope (`with_seed` names the rebinding). It's checked by a differential against a hand fold (1,500 generated inputs plus prefixes) and the head law over a fold. No compiler grammar uses `@fold` yet: postfix adopts it in landing B, after a seed refresh.  **2. Operators read `op_symbol`** (lead-approved refinement of decision #3). The climb binds the word it took (`left`/`op`/`right`, `>>` as two tokens); `core.binop_of` is the one inverse of `op_symbol`, and `BinOp` is a Makes payload. A table word naming no operator is refused at assembly (exact golden). The spine's tables build `-> Expr.Binary` and `left "??" -> Expr.Coalesce` directly. **Dead:** `build_binary`, `build_bitwise`, `build_coalesce`, `bitwise_symbol`, the local `binop_of`. Still hand-built: `compare` (waits on `Is` keeping its pattern), `pipe`, `unmixed_bitwise`.  **3. `means()` step 1** (lane `nodes-operators`). `~x` is now a node, `Bitnot { rewrite }`, walked as its rewrite. It's tied by one verb, `store.mint_for`. A refusal inside the rewrite keeps its words and gains a frame at the sugar: "`~s` means `s ^ -1`" (golden). `avra expand` prints the same sentence. `fmt` now prints `~x`, where it used to rewrite your source into `x ^ -1` (a real lossless-format bug). A template test counts exactly one operand copy.  **4. The `Rewrite` quote kind** (`means()` landing 1): a quote whose holes are arena ids (`${self.value}`), with its own refusal for a non-id hole. Nothing reads it yet; landing 2 bakes each sugar's template lazily, after a seed refresh.  **Receipts (Sprites, each slice on its own tree):** `make avra` ×2; grammar 147/147; features/tests 202–209 + 29 programs; expr_spine 729–740; quote 134; core 318; nullable 421; fmt and idioms clean. column2: batch: a cancel outranks a task's own ready arm (#696) + cleanup that survives an unwind (#692) + after/quiet/every in @std/time (#713)
column3: One integration PR of two reviewed lane PRs, merged onto main after batch #707. One hand resolution: `runtime/tests/vtask_test.c` between #691 (landed) and #696 — both sides' cases kept; every mutation's text occurs exactly once (checked by script); `make runtime-tests` green on the merged tree (flow 276 checks, tick 14, vtasks 61, 0 failed).  - **#696** (flow-04p-38): a park ranks another party's claim, then a cancel, then a passed deadline, then the task's OWN claim; every 64 own-claim turns of a task, while a timer or descriptor waiter is filed, due timers fire and the poller is asked. A cancel is heard at turn 0 where it was never heard in 20M turns. Own-claim turn 9.6–11.9 ns → 12.1–13.6 ns (measured). Splits FLOW 01's `claim_before_cancel` pin as design P2 asks. - **#692** (flow-14e): release that lived only in an `.Err` arm moves to `defer`/`errdefer` (bounded where it waits) — net lookup and race, `Bell.waited`, the TLS handshake, https `tls_opened`, the pool's `dialed`, fetch's `lent`, a server connection, ws `opened_over`, process `serving`, sqlite `exhausted`. Each leak witnessed failing first under `t.cancel()`.  - **#713** (flow-04-time): `after(d)`, `quiet(d)`, `every(d)` as sealed values in `@std/time` with `wait()` — the first piece of the `select` slice; std-time 23/23, 9 programs, both engines.  - **#714** (flow-suite-reason): a test program that does not derive makes the suite's eval leg exit 3 with its report on stderr — never the verdict's exit 1 with the reason on stdout.  Closes #696, closes #692, closes #713, closes #714.  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
